questions.q: What must be true of the data before you can use binary search?
o: It must be sorted and allow random access
It must contain no duplicate values
It must be stored in a linked list
It must contain fewer than a thousand items
questions.w: Halving the range relies on the order, and jumping to the middle in O(1) needs an array or ArrayList.

questions.q: Why write mid as lo + (hi - lo) / 2 instead of (lo + hi) / 2?
o: The sum lo + hi can overflow an int on very large arrays
It makes the loop run twice as fast
It avoids sorting the array first
It is required for the array to have even length
questions.w: For indexes near Integer.MAX_VALUE the sum wraps to a negative number. The subtraction form cannot overflow.

questions.q: What does Arrays.binarySearch return when the key is missing?
o: -(insertion point) - 1, which is negative
0, meaning the first position
null
The index of the largest smaller element
questions.w: Any negative result means not found, and -result - 1 is the position where the key would be inserted to keep the array sorted.

questions.q: What does it mean for a sorting algorithm to be stable?
o: Equal elements keep their original relative order
It always runs in the same amount of time
It uses no extra memory
It never throws an exception
questions.w: Stability matters when sorting records by several keys in turn. Merge sort and TimSort are stable; quicksort and heap sort usually are not.

questions.q: Why is merge sort O(n log n) in every case?
o: There are about log n levels of splitting and each level does O(n) merge work
It sorts each element with a single comparison
It only compares neighbouring elements once
It never needs to merge two sorted halves
questions.w: The splits do not depend on the data, so the best, average and worst cases are the same.

questions.q: When does quicksort degrade to O(n²)?
o: When the pivot is repeatedly the smallest or largest element
When the array contains only distinct values
When the array has an even number of elements
When it is called recursively on both halves
questions.w: Extreme pivots create very unbalanced splits, for example always taking the first element of already sorted data. Random or median-of-three pivots avoid it.

questions.q: Which sort does Java use for List.sort and Arrays.sort on objects?
o: TimSort, a stable merge and insertion hybrid
Bubble sort
A dual-pivot quicksort that is not stable at all
Selection sort
questions.w: Primitive arrays use a dual-pivot quicksort; object sorts must be stable, so they use TimSort.

questions.q: You need the 10 largest values from a stream of millions. What is the better approach?
o: Keep a min-heap of size 10 and drop the smallest when it grows
Sort the whole stream and take the last 10
Store everything in a HashSet and scan it ten times
Use binary search on the unsorted stream
questions.w: A heap of size k costs O(n log k) time and O(k) memory, and works on data that does not fit in memory.
